title: Injective ring-sheaf differential sequence and its canonical quotient-resolution roof
statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space and $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\xrightarrow{j}\mathcal C$ maps of sheaves of commutative rings, with $j$ injective. Use the standard resolutions and alternating complexes $K$ of [lem-sfb-standard-sheaf-cotangent-flat-functorial-model]. Set $P=P^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B/\mathcal A)$, $Q=P^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal C/\mathcal A)$, $S=P^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal B/\mathcal B)$ and $R=P^{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal C/\mathcal B)$. With standard functoriality maps and augmentations, put $\overline Q=Q\otimes_P\mathcal B$ and $\overline R=R\otimes_S\mathcal B$, degreewise in sheaves. These agree with sheafification of the sectionwise tensor constructions. Before sheafification, on every open $U$, the quotient augmentations $Q(U)\otimes_{P(U)}\mathcal B(U)\to\mathcal C(U)$ and $R(U)\otimes_{S(U)}\mathcal B(U)\to\mathcal C(U)$, with $P(U),Q(U),R(U),S(U)$ here denoting the sectionwise standard polynomial resolutions before sheafification, are polynomial resolutions in the precise sense of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Their sheafified augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms on alternating complexes.
There is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of $\mathcal C$-modules
$$0\to K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C\xrightarrow{i}K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{q}T_Q\to0,\qquad T_Q=s(\Omega^1_{\overline Q/\mathcal B}\otimes_{\overline Q}\mathcal C).$$
The maps are induced by $P\to Q\to\overline Q$ and universal differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; $i$ is the canonical standard functoriality map. Put $T_R=s(\Omega^1_{\overline R/\mathcal B}\otimes_{\overline R}\mathcal C)$. The canonical maps
$$K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\alpha}T_R\xleftarrow{\beta}T_Q$$
induced by $R\to\overline R$ and $\overline Q\to\overline R$ are quasi-isomorphisms. In $D(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $\alpha^{-1}\beta:T_Q\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal B}$ carries $q$ to the canonical base-ring functoriality arrow $K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}\to K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal B}$. The sequence, roof and this equality commute with open restrictions. No flatness of $\mathcal C$ over $\mathcal B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08SZ (lemma-triangle-sheaves-rings), injective case, displayed differential sequence and canonical roof; Tags 08SD (remark-triangle) and 08SE (remark-explicit-map).

proof.text: Fix an open $U$ and write $A=\mathcal A(U)$, $B=\mathcal B(U)$, $C=\mathcal C(U)$. In Steps 1--5 all resolutions are sectionwise, before sheafification. The map $B\to C$ is injective. The recursive standard maps of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] identify the variable set of $P_n$ with a subset $X_n$ of the variable set $E_n$ of $Q_n$: for $n=0$ this is $B\hookrightarrow C$; inductively an injection of variable sets gives an injection of polynomial rings because distinct finitely supported monomial coefficient lists remain distinct. The resulting injection of underlying sets is the variable injection in the next degree. Put $Y_n=E_n\setminus X_n$. Thus $P_n=A[X_n]$, $Q_n=A[X_n\sqcup Y_n]=P_n[Y_n]$, with the actual standard map as the displayed inclusion. Tensoring its augmentation $P_n\to B$ gives $\overline Q_n=B[Y_n]$. The same argument with base ring $B$ gives the analogous description for $S_n\to R_n$. Complements are used only to check exactness, not to define any simplicial or restriction map.

source.place: Tag 08SD (remark-triangle), polynomiality of Q_n over P_n; Tag 08SE (remark-explicit-map), polynomiality of R_n over S_n.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-injective-standard-resolution-quotients] to $A\to B\hookrightarrow C$. It gives polynomiality, degreewise surjectivity to $C$, and the quasi-isomorphism $s(\overline Q)\to C[0]$. Apply the same node a second time to $B\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}B\hookrightarrow C$, whose two standard resolutions are precisely $S$ and $R$. It gives the same three properties for $\overline R$. These are exactly the polynomial-resolution hypotheses of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]; no flatness of $B\to C$ occurs in either application.

source.place: Tags 08SD and 08SE, quotient-resolution input; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), polynomial-resolution convention.

proof.text: In degree $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] over $A$ to $P_n=A[X_n]$ and $Q_n=A[X_n\sqcup Y_n]$, and over $B$ to $\overline Q_n=B[Y_n]$, always tensoring coefficients to $C$. The three differential modules are respectively $\bigoplus_{X_n}C$, $\bigoplus_{X_n\sqcup Y_n}C$, and $\bigoplus_{Y_n}C$. The universal differential maps [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] make the first arrow inclusion of the $X_n$ coordinates and the second projection onto $Y_n$: an old variable maps into $B$, so its relative $B$-differential is zero; a new variable maps to its namesake. An element in the kernel of the projection has zero $Y_n$ coordinates and is therefore the image of its finitely supported $X_n$ coordinates; inclusion is injective, and extending a $Y_n$ vector by zeros proves surjectivity. Thus the sequence is split exact without flatness of $C$ over $B$. The maps themselves are induced by $P\to Q\to\overline Q$, not by the chosen complements, and commute with all faces and degeneracies by their universal derivation formulas. Taking alternating faces therefore gives a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes before sheafification.

source.place: Tag 08SD, displayed differential sequence; Algebra Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), with the same finite-support argument for arbitrary variable sets.

proof.text: The standard square maps in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] give $P\to S$, $Q\to R$ for change of base $A\to B$, with $P\to Q\to R=P\to S\to R$ and with all augmentations commuting. Hence the tensor universal property gives $h:\overline Q\to\overline R$, explicitly $q\otimes b\mapsto f(q)\otimes b$ where $f:Q\to R$. The relation $p q\otimes b=q\otimes\epsilon_P(p)b$ is preserved because $f(p)$ is the image of $p$ in $S$ and $\epsilon_S(f(p))=\epsilon_P(p)$. Its augmentation satisfies $\epsilon_{\overline R}h(q\otimes b)=\epsilon_R(f(q))j(b)=\epsilon_Q(q)j(b)=\epsilon_{\overline Q}(q\otimes b)$. For a face or degeneracy $\theta$, both $\theta h$ and $h\theta$ send $q\otimes b$ to $f(\theta q)\otimes b$, since $f$ is simplicial and $B$ is constant. Hence $h$ is an augmented simplicial $B$-algebra map over $C$. Together with $g:R\to\overline R$, $r\mapsto r\otimes1$, it induces the two chain maps $\alpha$ and $\beta$ on relative $B$-differentials tensored to $C$; their formula is $\mathrm dz\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm d(\text{image of }z)\otimes c$, by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Tag 08SE, commutative diagram and the resulting canonical map Q_bar to R_bar.

proof.text: The standard augmentation $R\to C$ is a polynomial resolution by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], and Step 2 supplies this hypothesis for $\overline Q\to C$ and $\overline R\to C$. Apply that node's comparison isomorphisms and their naturality to the two augmented $B$-algebra maps $g$ and $h$ of Step 4. For either map the comparison of the target differential complex with $L_{C/B}$, composed with the induced map, equals the comparison of the source with $L_{C/B}$. Both comparisons are isomorphisms. Hence $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are isomorphisms in $D(C)$, where $L_{C/B}$ lives. Since cohomology factors through localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their cohomology maps are isomorphisms, so they are quasi-isomorphisms. The maps and all three complexes are $C$-linear. Their kernels, images and cohomology have the same underlying $B$-modules after restriction of scalars, since those submodules and quotients are computed on the same elements. Each cohomology map is therefore a bijective $C$-linear map $u$. Its inverse is $C$-linear: applying injective $u$ to $u^{-1}(cx)$ and $c u^{-1}(x)$ gives $cx$ in both cases. Thus both roof maps are quasi-isomorphisms over $C$.

source.place: Tag 08SE, final roof; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), canonical comparison for arbitrary polynomial resolutions.

proof.text: Perform Steps 1--5 on all opens and sheafify the actual canonical maps. By [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], the free sheaf algebra and the standard differential complexes are the sheafified sectionwise constructions. The simplicial sheaf algebras themselves are sheafified sectionwise standard resolutions, by induction on $n$: $\mathcal P_0$ is the sheafified sectionwise algebra $U\mapsto\mathcal A(U)[\mathcal B(U)]$; if the sectionwise $P_{n-1}$ sheafifies to $\mathcal P_{n-1}$ as rings, then by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] the underlying sheaf of sets $|\mathcal P_{n-1}|$ is the set-sheafification of $|P_{n-1}|$. For a presheaf of sets $G$, maps of sheaves of $\mathcal A$-algebras out of the sheafified sectionwise polynomial algebra $(U\mapsto\mathcal A(U)[G(U)])^\#$ are, by the universal properties of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and of polynomial algebras, maps of presheaves of sets out of $G$, hence out of $G^\#$. So the sheafified algebras on $|P_{n-1}|$ and on $|\mathcal P_{n-1}|$ agree, i.e. $P_n$ sheafifies to $\mathcal P_n=\mathcal A[|\mathcal P_{n-1}|]$. Faces, degeneracies, augmentations and the standard maps are given by the same evaluation and unit formulas on both sides, so they correspond. The same holds for $Q,R,S$.

source.place: Tag 08SZ (lemma-triangle-sheaves-rings), presheaf-then-sheafify paragraph; sites-modules.tex Tags 08TP (lemma-differentials-sheafify), 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), 03CN and 03CO.

proof.text: With the algebras identified as in Step 6, by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor], sheafification of each degreewise tensor $Q\otimes_P B$ and $R\otimes_S B$ is respectively the specified sheaf tensor $\overline Q$ and $\overline R$; the algebra multiplications agree since both send $(q\otimes b)(q'\otimes b')$ to $qq'\otimes bb'$. By [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel], sectionwise relative differentials sheafify to the relative sheaf differentials, preserving their universal derivations. Applying the tensor comparison again identifies the terms of Step 3. For the first term, the balanced maps $(\mathrm dp\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm dp\otimes bc$ and $\mathrm dp\otimes c\mapsto(\mathrm dp\otimes1)\otimes c$ identify $(\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B)\otimes_B C$ with $\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P C$; they are inverse and commute with faces. Thus its sheafification is exactly $K_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C$. The same comparisons identify Step 5's roof with $\alpha,\beta$. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] preserves the degreewise exact sequence. It also preserves these quasi-isomorphisms and the two quotient augmentations: it preserves kernels, images and cokernels, so sheafified cohomology is the sheafification of the sectionwise cohomology. This proves all the asserted sheaf exactness and quasi-isomorphism clauses.

source.place: Tag 08SZ (lemma-triangle-sheaves-rings), presheaf-then-sheafify paragraph; sites-modules.tex Tags 08TP (lemma-differentials-sheafify), 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), 03CN and 03CO.

proof.text: Let $v:K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal A}\to K_{\mathcal C/\mathcal B}$ be the standard base-ring functoriality map of [lem-sfb-standard-sheaf-cotangent-flat-functorial-model]. The square in Step 4 gives an equality of ring maps $Q\to\overline Q\xrightarrow h\overline R=Q\xrightarrow f R\xrightarrow g\overline R$: both send $q$ to $f(q)\otimes1$. On each generating differential $\mathrm dq\otimes c$, both $\beta q$ and $\alpha v$ therefore give $\mathrm d(f(q)\otimes1)\otimes c$. Universal differentials generate the modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], so $\beta q=\alpha v$ as chain maps, before and after sheafification. In $D(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] invert $\alpha$ to obtain $\alpha^{-1}\beta q=v$. The first arrow of the short exact sequence is likewise exactly the standard arrow: it sends $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(\text{image of }p)\otimes c$, the formula in the flat functorial model node. This identifies both arrows, including the required quotient-arrow comparison.

source.place: Tags 08SE and 08SZ, the arrow-compatible roof; Tag 08SS, standard functoriality maps.

proof.text: For an inclusion of opens $V\subseteq U$, restriction is a commutative square of ring maps on sections. The strict composition property of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] makes every square between $P,Q,S,R$ commute with that restriction. On quotients the map is $z\otimes b\mapsto z|_V\otimes b|_V$; on differentials it is $\mathrm dz\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm d(z|_V)\otimes c|_V$. These formulas commute with $g,h$, both differential arrows, and the equality of Step 8. Their sheafifications are the same maps by the natural tensor and differential identifications [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor, lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel]. Finally, a commuting square with an invertible $\alpha$ also commutes with its inverse, by multiplying the square by the inverses. For restriction to an open subspace $V\subseteq T$: on every open $W\subseteq V$ the sectionwise rings, resolutions, tensors, differential modules and maps of Steps 1--5 for $\mathcal A|_V\to\mathcal B|_V\to\mathcal C|_V$ are literally those for $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ on $W$, so the presheaf data on $V$ are the restrictions of the presheaf data on $T$. The inclusion of the opens of $V$ into the opens of $T$ is continuous and cocontinuous, so by [lem-sp-module-slice-sheafification-independent-ring] module sheafification commutes with this restriction, naturally and compatibly with the sheafification units. Hence the restricted sheaf sequence, roof and the arrows of Step 8 are the ones built from the restricted rings. Thus the sequence, roof, derived identification and arrow equality commute with open restrictions. No naturality of the auxiliary complements $Y_n$ is needed.
